hints: Both lists are sorted. If you fix an item a[i], which partner from b gives its cheapest combo, and which one comes next?
Treat each a[i] as a sorted row a[i]+b[0], a[i]+b[1], … and merge the rows with a min-heap that stores (total, i, j).

1. Push (a[i]+b[0], i, 0) for the first min(len(a), k) rows.
  2. Repeat k times: pop the smallest (total, i, j) and record total.
  3. If j+1 < b.length, push (a[i]+b[j+1], i, j+1).
  4. Return the recorded totals.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Generate all a.length × b.length totals, sort them, take the first k.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: K-way merge of the rows with a min-heap; only about k + rows entries are ever pushed.

explain: For a = [1,4,9], b = [2,3,10], k = 4 the heap starts with 3 (1+2), 6 (4+2), 11 (9+2). Pop 3 and push 1+3 = 4; pop 4 and push 1+10 = 11; pop 6 and push 4+3 = 7; pop 7. The answer is [3,4,6,7]. It works because each row is sorted, so the next candidate from a row is always just one step right of what was popped. Edge case: b may have only one item, so check j+1 < b.length before pushing.
recognize: Two sorted lists and 'k smallest pair sums' → merge sorted rows with a min-heap.
